# Metrics and alerts

Generated from two sources that only agree with each other because this page checks it: the Prometheus metrics the operator and the world sync node agent actually register, read from their registries rather than from source, so this table can't drift from what is really exported; and the alerting rules in `charts/spawnery/templates/prometheusrule.yaml`, rendered through `helm template` because that file is a Helm chart template, not YAML, until Helm has expanded it.

## Metrics

The `spawnery_worldsync_` metrics come from the world sync node agents on port 8090, the rest from the operator on port 8080.

## Alerts

Off by default (`metrics.prometheusRule.enabled: false`, see [chart values](chart-values.md)); rendered here with that value and `worldSync.enabled` turned on and every other value left at the chart's own default. The `spawnery-worldsync` group renders only with world sync on. `SpawneryCAExpiringSoon`'s summary interpolates `metrics.prometheusRule.caExpiryWarningDays` -- the number in it below is that value's chart *default*, not a fixed part of the alert; an install that overrides it gets a different number in that one message.

### SpawneryAgentConnectionsRefused

**Group:** <code>spawnery-agents</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>15m</code>

The spawnery operator is refusing agent connections over the per-peer bound.

```
increase(spawnery_agent_connections_refused_total{bound="peer"}[15m]) > 0
```

One peer address has held MaxConnectionsPerPeer connections open and asked for more. Find the peer in the operator&#x27;s log -- it is logged at the first refusal and then at every power of ten, so the line is there without the log being the flood. Compare spawnery_agent_open_connections against spawnery_agents_expected: a fleet at its pod count with one peer refusing is a single misbehaving pod, and a fleet well above it is something else.

### SpawneryAgentFleetOverItsBound

**Group:** <code>spawnery-agents</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>critical</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>5m</code>

The spawnery agent endpoint holds more connections than its fleet can account for.

```
increase(spawnery_agent_connections_refused_total{bound="fleet"}[15m]) > 0
```

This is the one bound in the agent channel that is a statement about the fleet rather than about one peer. Reaching it means either that several pods are opening connections they have no use for, or that addresses which are not managed pods at all are reaching the endpoint -- the NetworkPolicy admits any pod labelled spawnery.cloud/managed-by and does not count them. Start with the peers in the operator&#x27;s log and check each against `kubectl get pod -A -o wide`. A spawnery_agents_expected of 0 beside a fleet that plainly is not empty is the third reading: the count itself is broken, and the endpoint is serving one peer&#x27;s worth while it is.

### SpawneryCAExpiringSoon

**Group:** <code>spawnery-ca</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>1h</code>

The spawnery agent CA expires in under 90 days.

```
(spawnery_ca_expiry_timestamp_seconds - time())
  < 7776000
```

Rotating it is a deliberate multi-step procedure with a hold in the middle that waits for a person, so start it with time in hand. Annotate the operator&#x27;s TLS secret with spawnery.cloud/rotate-ca=start and follow docs/reference/known-issues.md&#x27;s &quot;On the agent channel&quot; section. Note that a start annotation can sit unread for up to an hour on an idle cluster, because the operator only re-reads it on its slow tick.

### SpawneryCARotationBlocked

**Group:** <code>spawnery-ca</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>6h</code>

A spawnery CA rotation has been waiting on namespaces for six hours.

```
spawnery_ca_rotation_blocked_namespaces > 0
```

Read spawnery.cloud/ca-rotation-blocked-on on the operator&#x27;s TLS secret for the names. A namespace with leftover agent pods and no Network blocks the gate by design; the remedy is to delete or drain those groups.

### SpawneryCARotationStalled

**Group:** <code>spawnery-ca</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>24h</code>

A spawnery CA rotation has been distributing for a day.

```
spawnery_ca_rotation_phase{phase="distributing"} == 1
```

The gate waits for every namespace to show the incoming CA and then for a projection margin plus the agent session deadline -- a quarter of an hour in total, not a day. Check spawnery.cloud/ca-rotation-blocked-on, and spawnery.cloud/ca-rotation-discarded for a slot the operator repaired or threw away.

### SpawneryOperatorMissingPermissions

**Group:** <code>spawnery-permissions</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>critical</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>5m</code>

The spawnery operator lacks {{ $value }} permission(s) it needs ({{ $labels.scope }}).

```
spawnery_permissions_missing > 0
```

The operator&#x27;s log names each missing verb and the call site that needs it -- search it for &quot;is missing permissions it needs&quot;. It keeps running on purpose, because a missing permission may be one this cluster&#x27;s paths never take, so nothing else will look wrong: the paths that need the verb simply reconcile nothing. Compare the ClusterRole and Role in the release against config/rbac/role.yaml, and check that the bindings still name the operator&#x27;s ServiceAccount.

### SpawneryServingCertificateNotRenewing

**Group:** <code>spawnery-ca</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>critical</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>1h</code>

The spawnery operator&#x27;s serving certificate expires within a day.

```
(spawnery_serving_cert_expiry_timestamp_seconds - time()) < 86400
```

This certificate renews on its own once a third of its life is left, so reaching one day means the renewal path has stopped. Every agent handshake fails when it expires.

### SpawneryWorldDownloadFailed

**Group:** <code>spawnery-worldsync</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code></code>

A world download on node {{ $labels.node }} failed.

```
increase(spawnery_worldsync_download_failures_total[15m]) > 0
```

The pod that waited for it failed its start. The agent&#x27;s log has the error (&quot;download failed&quot;); an object the manifest names but the bucket lacks means the world in the bucket is damaged.

### SpawneryWorldLeaseConflicts

**Group:** <code>spawnery-worldsync</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>15m</code>

Node {{ $labels.node }} has refused a world for 15 minutes because another node holds its lease.

```
increase(spawnery_worldsync_lease_conflicts_total[5m]) > 0
```

A pod waits in ContainerCreating with an Unavailable event naming the node that holds the world. That node&#x27;s agent still renews the lease: either a pod there still mounts the world, or its final upload cannot finish.

### SpawneryWorldOrphaned

**Group:** <code>spawnery-worldsync</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code></code>

Node {{ $labels.node }} moved a world&#x27;s local copy to orphans/.

```
increase(spawnery_worldsync_orphans_total[30m]) > 0
```

The node lost the world&#x27;s lease while it still held changes the bucket does not have. The copy lies under orphans/ in the node directory (worldSync.hostPath) and never uploads; the agent&#x27;s log names the world. Compare it with what the bucket holds before restoring anything by hand.

### SpawneryWorldSnapshotsPending

**Group:** <code>spawnery-worldsync</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **Severity:** <code>warning</code> &nbsp;&nbsp; **For:** <code>10m</code>

Snapshots on node {{ $labels.node }} have not reached the bucket for 10 minutes.

```
max by (node, pod) (spawnery_worldsync_pending_snapshots) > 0
```

The node agent keeps retrying, and its log says why (&quot;retrying&quot;). Usually the object store is unreachable or refuses the credentials. Play since the last upload exists only on this node until then; if a stopped world&#x27;s lease goes stale meanwhile, another node may start it from the last upload and this copy moves to orphans/.
